perspective:
Vincent’s available information:

- He knows he is Vincent Chinana, an Alaska Native mechanic with a middle-school education. He knows Patrick Guzman as a Latino construction worker and long-time friend from their teenage years; they share a blue-collar bond and have often collaborated, combining Vincent’s mechanical skills with Patrick’s construction expertise.

- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick considering a new construction venture. Patrick says it seems like a good opportunity, that he thinks it is worth the risk, but that he is still weighing options. Vincent says he has heard it is risky, asks if Patrick is sure, worries it could jeopardize financial security, and suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick thanks him and says he will think it over more.

- Over the next few days, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion of the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent says he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and that he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says that as a friend he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologizes, admits he should have been more open, and agrees to sit down and explain everything.

- During their detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns the situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and expresses gratitude for the support.

- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent has/learns new information indicating the venture might actually turn a profit. He tells Patrick this. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier, proposes a joint venture, and says he now sees potential. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.

- At Vincent’s house, Vincent is optimistic about their joint venture. He says that combining their skills can make it a success and wants to start drafting a business plan, outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees that they should cover all bases and set it up for success.
